messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT created: Sev2 - KV cache memory spike / continuous-batching perf cliff (1829533000)
oncall-bot: Pager: @alex.k (primary) @samir (backup) — runbook: /incidents/continuous-batch-kv
alex.k: saw huge memory churn on runtime-3 starting ~11:01 UTC, latency 95p jumped from 120ms -> 2.3s. errors: 504s on long-chat routes.
samir: noticing lots of cache-evict logs and TTL churn. looks like a single tenant generated many long prefixes. possible misconfig of batching params?
maria_g: customer reports intermittent truncation on streaming responses. ticket #CS-7984 linked.
ops_sre: confirmed spike: node gpu-12 memory at 98%, OOMs avoided via eviction but throughput tanked. suspect max_batch_tokens was set to 65k in last deploy.
eng-ml: that seems wrong — default is 2048. who applied 65k?
alex.k: checking deploy audit... `redwoodctl config get runtime/continuous-batching`
alex.k: audit shows last change 1829532900 by automated rollout script from performance-experiments pipeline.
samir: we need immediate mitigation: 2-step: 1) reduce max_batch_tokens to 4096 2) set max_num_seqs to 8 3) throttle long-chat traffic. can we patch live?
ops_sre: agree. prepping hotpatch. applying via `redwoodctl config set continuous-batching.max_batch_tokens=4096`
ops_sre: applying now…
ops_sre: `OK` — pushing to runtime config, notifying runtime instances to pick up config.
eng-ml: also suggest increasing per-request timeout to avoid requests accumulating in KV cache windows. set `request.timeout_ms=120000` temporarily.
alex.k: I'll open a temporary route policy to route long-chat traffic to lower-throughput pool (dedicated-fallback-1) to protect hosts.
alex.k: `redwoodctl route add-policy --route long-chat --fallback dedicated-fallback-1 --limit 20%`
ops_sre: restart not required; config reloads in ~30s. watching metrics.
(30s pass)
ops_sre: memory falling on gpu-12 -> 67%. tail latency improving. 95p down to 210ms. no new OOMs.
maria_g: customer CS-7984 updated: partial functionality restored, streaming stable but with occasional truncation, they accept degraded perf for now. :white_check_mark:
samir: need to patch automation that pushed 65k. hit a bad experiment config. I've muted that experiment and opened PR to validate upper bounds.
eng-ml: postmortem items: add validation to config deployer to reject max_batch_tokens > 16384 and max_num_seqs > 64. also add an anomaly alert on cache-evict-rate > 1000/min.
ops_sre: creating follow-up runbook entry for hotpatch steps and fallback route commands.
alex.k: customer impact: 3 customers affected briefly, CS tickets created: CS-7984, CS-7989, CS-7992. Notified account teams.
support-bot: auto-created incident timeline ticket IT-31245 and linked CS tickets.
eng-ml: quick log snippet from runtime-3 around spike:
```
[11:01:12] kvcache: insert_seq tenant=tenant-42 seq_len=64000 prefix_key=...
[11:01:13] kvcache: evict_count=3421 total_entries=987654
[11:01:13] batcher: queued_tokens=65328 active_batches=120
[11:01:14] runtime: latency_p95=2300ms error=504
```
alex.k: timeline: change rolled at 11:01, alert at 11:03, hotpatch applied 11:08, stable by 11:12.
samir: recommend follow-ups: limit experiments that change batching without canary to 1 host, add pre-deploy config lint, and alerting on sudden increase in queued_tokens and eviction rate.
maria_g: I'll draft customer-facing note outlining cause (misconfigured batching params -> KV cache thrash) and mitigation.
ops_sre: final action: keep reduced limits for 24h, run capture of workload traces for root-cause analysis, schedule incident review tomorrow.
alex.k: thanks team. adding everyone to postmortem thread. closing alert unless we see regression. :thumbsup:
